Murray Assassination

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Cloete Murray and his son Thomas were gunned down in a hit on Saturday. Who wanted them dead and why. We follow up on the Masters office and the high profile cases Murray was investigating

Unique Selling Point:
We have the last interview done with Murray, the inside track from the suspended acting master whose legal battles with the department of justice continue, and we have the trust of the people who knew him and what he was working on and they are prepared to speak to us

Summary:
In April 2022 Carte Blanche tried to unravel what was happening in the higher echelons of the Masters office. Deputy Master Christene Rossouw was suspended on what she claimed were trumped up charges and Acting Chief Master Tessie Bezuidenhout was also suspended. At the heart of the matter it seemed was the appointment of liquidator Cloete Murray on the Bosasa matter and the role played in that appointment by Rossouw and Bezuidenhout. Murray had fought and won several attempts to remove him, and continued doing his work asking the difficult questions, as he put it. Christene left the department of justice and took early retirement. She says she just didn’t have what it took to fight powerful but shadowy interests that were trying to capture the masters office. From that time until last week, suspended acting chief master Tessie Bezuidenhout has been embroiled in a protracted disciplinary process to clear her name and get her job back. In the interim the chief Master Mafojane literally disappeared from his job on Feb 1st and took sick leave. The new acting chief master Penelope Roberts is allegedly captured and has used her time to try and remove Cloete Murray from liquidations he was busy with, as well as adding extraneous liquidators to old cases so that they can benefit from the fees unnecessarily. Welcome to state capture reloaded. Masters office style. We have four examples of this already. The very thing that Tessie Bezuidenhout was fighting against is now happening in the masters office. As John Walker her attorney told Carte Blanche – control the masters office and you control the liquidations. Cloete meanwhile has continued his work on a number of high profile and contentious cases – The confidential 417 inquiry into Bosasa has reached a point where there is an interim report, that we are told calls for further investigations into some high profile people. He was also working on an Investec case where the bank is owed millions.

Further information:
Then came Saturday the 18th March. Cloete Murray and his son Thomas were driving back to Pretoria and just past the New Road offramp travelling north, they were attacked by gun wielding assassins whose bullets ripped through the car and killed his son Thomas on the scene. Cloete Murray was rushed to hospital but died later from two bullets to the head.

The killers fled and to date it seems that in yet another assassination, they will go free.
The killings have sent shockwaves through the legal fraternity and prompted questions about who did this and why.
Stand in line and buy a ticket says Kobus Van Niekerk, Murray’s attorney and family spokesperson. He had a lot of enemies.

Probably the obvious answer is money and power. Because Murray separates bad boys from their cash, and no- one likes that. Some have speculated its Bosasa, others say our story was spot on and this was just a continuation of the attempts to capture the masters office. Either way a brazen and chilling message has been sent to liquidators and its working. People are terrified to speak out. Tessie Bezuidenhout and John Walker now have security when they move around. Even if Bezuidenhout wins her case, and Walker is convinced she will, will it be safe enough for her to return to work? Because Bezuidenhout is more senior to the current master and would likely replace her, spoiling the plans of the so called capturers.

Carte Blanche goes back to those on the frontlines of this story and tries to find some answers, as another assassination is added to South Africa’s grim tally of unsolved murders.

Final Script: Murray and Son. TX Sunday 26th March 2023

Voice over one
The 18th March 2023. A hot, late summer afternoon in Gauteng.

Cloete Murray, the liquidator known for winding up some of the country’s biggest state capture cases amongst many other multi million rand matters, was driving northwards with his son Thomas.

Then came chaos.

Just beyond the New Road offramp in Midrand, assassins let loose their violence.

An assault rifle aimed directly at Murray and his son

Link
This was done with precision and expertise. These assassins don’t miss. Nine bullets pummeled the car with the final shots penetrating the drivers headrest. The brutality of it all- unspeakable

Voice over 2
The vehicle eventually came to a standstill about 50 meters from the bridge. Thomas Murray died on the scene.

His father- succumbed to the bullets, a few hours later in hospital.

Fade to black

Voice over 3
The hit has sent shockwaves through the legal and insolvency fraternity. Most retreated into their fear. Few were prepared to speak out

John Walker
I think the entire industry is in shock at the moment. Are we at a point in this country where the law no longer matters because the people that try to enforce the law, them and their families are now personal targets.

Voice over 4
In April 2022 we spoke to Attorney John Walker. His clients Christene Rossouw and Tessie Bezuidenhout were both senior officials at the Masters office that oversees liquidations and deceased estates.

They had appointed Cloete to the liquidation of Bosasa, an infamous company enmeshed in state capture

That decision cost them their reputations and their jobs when the justice department suspended them.

Bongani
So the masters that appointed Murray are out of the way, now he is out of the way?
John
That is where we are. That is where we are now.

Voice over 5
Bosasa may not be the reason for his death, but it’s no secret the directors wanted Cloete Murray off the case

The television interview we conducted with Murray was his last.

Bongani
Is state capture over?
Cloete Murray
No, most certainly not. People often think now that the Zondo commission is over these people will just go away. They won’t. They are fighting, there’s most certainly still some residual evidence of state capture in the system

Voice over 6
Attempts to remove Murray from the Bosasa liquidation went right up to the Supreme court of appeal. But the court found Cloete Murray stays.

Cloete
I am known to be an astute liquidator, I investigate matters properly and I think I probably ask the wrong questions

Voice over 7
Also in Murray’s portfolio was the liquidation of Trillian, another controversial company responsible for looting millions from Eskom and Transnet

Cloete Murray
It’s going to take a number of years to investigate these matters, but ultimately we as a country need to deal with this, we can fight it, but it’s not over by any stretch of the imagination.
Bongani
So would you say that more that you dig, the more powerful or connected individuals possibly stand to lose?
Cloete
Yes, if people benefitted from corruption its likely come out in the 417 inquiry.

Voice over 8
A 417 inquiry is a legal process for liquidators to probe the affairs of a company, establish director liability, and recover money

Link
So who would want Cloete Murray out of the way, well as one source said to us, take a ticket and stand in line. Over a long career he had made some very powerful enemies

Bongani
I asked Cloete Murray this question, often politicians will give a defence, they will say where is the smoking gun, it’s clear now that he had a lot of smoking guns?
John Walker
Not only that bear in mind the 417 Inquiry is a really powerful tool. You as a witness are forced to answer all questions even those that incriminate you. If you are subpoenaed to a 417 you are laid bare, your transactions are laid bare, everything you have done, every cent you have received they want to know why you received it and if you didn’t get it lawfully then you must pay it back

Voice over 9
As the 417 on Bosasa continued, the former acting chief master Tessie Bezuidenhout spent the year in a legal battle with the department of justice, with the aim of getting her job back here at the masters office.

Before he died, according to Walker, Murray called her

John Walker
Cloete contacted us last Tuesday. He indicated that he was about to finish or proceed with the section 417 inquiry. Well his words were that he was on the cusp of subpoenaing various prominent politicians to come and testify at that inquiry
Bongani
Was he able to indicate to you and Tessie who those prominent people were?
John Walker
Yes he did, but you must excuse me, with his murder, I am not at liberty to divulge those
Bongani
Is it about ...?
John Walker
Its members of cabinet, in certain instances, its high ranking government officials

Voice over 10
The police were back at the crime scene on Wednesday. If they have any clues they aren’t saying. But exposed in this shocking recording leaked to us, is that Cloete Murray’s death came as no surprise. Karen Keevy recorded here is talking to a fellow liquidator

Karen Keevy
I can’t believe it took so long. I was like when, when ok boom now.
Johan Engelbrecht
It’s not the right way, it’s not how you sort things out. It doesn’t work like that?
Karen
Sometimes, it’s the only way ... It was a matter of time and we all knew it


Voice over 11
She criticizes Cloete for winding down Bosasa too quickly when there were lucrative fees to be made.

Karen
You can run that thing for three years. While the 417 continues. Imagine the fees that you can make, but no, fuckface decides, bull in a China shop attitude, it reminds me of the Apartheid people the Afrikaners, the men who were in control of this country, it reminds me of that

Voice over 12
But most chilling she implies she has information about Cloete’s killers

Karen
I am saying to you it wasn’t the ANC, it wasn’t Bosasa, it wasn’t the Gupta’s. They are still sitting and wondering what they are going to do... It was our people ...The shooter was a white person, the instructor was a white person.

New VO ROR
When we contacted Karen Keevy on Friday evening she blamed alcohol for her comments and said her conversation was just her opinion, and she has no evidence to back up her claims

Karen Keevy
Say to John Walker he must make sure he is safe .

Voice over 13
John Walker upped his security after he received a disappearing warning on a messaging app saying simply 1 by 1

Bongani
As in we going to get you?
John
I have to make my own conclusions, I thought it was a prank. I don’t know what to read into that – this is Saturday evening before I knew about Cloete murder
Bongani
John that says you are next?
You know my mind says to me it’s not a movie, it’s ridiculous, I don’t want me to be the centre of this thing.

Voice over 14
Tessie Bezuidenhout and Christene Rossouw have not given up their fight for justice. They believe they were wrongfully suspended. But they are now wary and nervous


Bongani
Do you believe you are a target?
Christene
I have fears yes.

Voice over 15
And not without reason. She alleges the lawyer acting against her on behalf of the department sent her a link to the news of Cloete’s murder

Christene
There was nothing said, it was just the link
Bongani
This is the lawyer for the opposing side
Christene
Yes so it would be unethical of him to communicate with me without my attorneys permission.
Bongani
Saying have a look at how this guy died?
Yes
Bongani
How do you sleep after that?
Christene
You sleep with your one eye open

John Walker
You will remember the last time I spoke to you, I said the only people who investigate corporate fraud are liquidators. Their job is to recover the money’s that were unlawfully siphoned off and we are talking hundreds of millions of rands

Voice over 16
Several sources have suggested to us that the new acting chief master is making arbitrary appointments of liquidators in matters that are years old, simply so they can benefit from the fees.

Bongani
Is the masters office right now, captured?
John
In my view absolutely. You now have arbitrary appointment, liquidators that are added to estates – no reason given. Cloete himself was removed from an estate by the Pretoria masters office without any reasons being given.

Voice over 17
So is state capture being repeated at the Master’s office? And who will step into the breach in place of Cloete Murray, and as the list of assassinations grows longer, will his killers ever be brought to book?

The early signs, though, aren’t good: investigative journalist Kyle Cowan, found this file of an important case Cloete and Thomas were working on, in their bullet- riddled car- a sign that the police investigation has already been bungled.

THE END 10 56


PROMO ONE
Cloete Murray, a liquidator who told us he asked difficult questions, was assassinated last Saturday afternoon on the N1 highway with his son Thomas.

PROMO TWO 21

Voice over
Before his murder, Cloete Murray was about to subpoena some very powerful people

Bongani
Was he able to indicate to you and Tessie who those prominent people were?
John Walker
Yes he did, but you must excuse me, with his murder, I am not at liberty to divulge those
Bongani
Is it about ...?
John Walker
Its members of cabinet, in certain instances, its high ranking government officials

PROMO THREE 21

Voice over
Cloete Murrays liquidation portfolio included some of South Africa’s most notorious financial crime. But his murder with his son, has sent shockwaves through the legal and insolvency fraternity

John Walker
I think the entire industry is in shock at the moment. Are we at a point in this country where the law no longer matters because the people that try to enforce the law, them and their families are now personal targets.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Cloete Murray and his son Thomas were gunned down in a hit on Saturday. Who wanted them dead and why. We follow up on the Masters office and the high profile cases Murray was investigating
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have the last interview done with Murray, the inside track from the suspended acting master whose legal battles with the department of justice continue, and we have the trust of the people who knew him and what he was working on and they are prepared to speak to us
metadata.Summary: In April 2022 Carte Blanche tried to unravel what was happening in the higher echelons of the Masters office. Deputy Master Christene Rossouw was suspended on what she claimed were trumped up charges and Acting Chief Master Tessie Bezuidenhout was also suspended. At the heart of the matter it seemed was the appointment of liquidator Cloete Murray on the Bosasa matter and the role played in that appointment by Rossouw and Bezuidenhout. Murray had fought and won several attempts to remove him, and continued doing his work asking the difficult questions, as he put it. Christene left the department of justice and took early retirement. She says she just didn’t have what it took to fight powerful but shadowy interests that were trying to capture the masters office. From that time until last week, suspended acting chief master Tessie Bezuidenhout has been embroiled in a protracted disciplinary process to clear her name and get her job back. In the interim the chief Master Mafojane literally disappeared from his job on Feb 1st and took sick leave. The new acting chief master Penelope Roberts is allegedly captured and has used her time to try and remove Cloete Murray from liquidations he was busy with, as well as adding extraneous liquidators to old cases so that they can benefit from the fees unnecessarily. Welcome to state capture reloaded. Masters office style. We have four examples of this already. The very thing that Tessie Bezuidenhout was fighting against is now happening in the masters office. As John Walker her attorney told Carte Blanche – control the masters office and you control the liquidations. Cloete meanwhile has continued his work on a number of high profile and contentious cases – The confidential 417 inquiry into Bosasa has reached a point where there is an interim report, that we are told calls for further investigations into some high profile people. He was also working on an Investec case where the bank is owed millions.
metadata.Further information: Then came Saturday the 18th March. Cloete Murray and his son Thomas were driving back to Pretoria and just past the New Road offramp travelling north, they were attacked by gun wielding assassins whose bullets ripped through the car and killed his son Thomas on the scene. Cloete Murray was rushed to hospital but died later from two bullets to the head. The killers fled and to date it seems that in yet another assassination, they will go free. The killings have sent shockwaves through the legal fraternity and prompted questions about who did this and why. Stand in line and buy a ticket says Kobus Van Niekerk, Murray’s attorney and family spokesperson. He had a lot of enemies. Probably the obvious answer is money and power. Because Murray separates bad boys from their cash, and no- one likes that. Some have speculated its Bosasa, others say our story was spot on and this was just a continuation of the attempts to capture the masters office. Either way a brazen and chilling message has been sent to liquidators and its working. People are terrified to speak out. Tessie Bezuidenhout and John Walker now have security when they move around. Even if Bezuidenhout wins her case, and Walker is convinced she will, will it be safe enough for her to return to work? Because Bezuidenhout is more senior to the current master and would likely replace her, spoiling the plans of the so called capturers. Carte Blanche goes back to those on the frontlines of this story and tries to find some answers, as another assassination is added to South Africa’s grim tally of unsolved murders.
